description: Write, find and connect notes, keep a portable vault, and choose web or local editing.
text:
Try it without an account Open the public editor to try Markdown, preview and optional Vim. The scratchpad lives in the tab; this example does not save it to a private account. Download anything you want to keep before leaving.
Explore the public graph for an original six-note sample. It does not read private notes or start a processing job.
Create a private workspace Open the sign-in page , or create an email account . Complete the security check, follow the email link, then choose your name and passphrase. No account is created until you submit that confirmation form. Email links expire after 30 minutes and work once.
Verified email/password accounts can request a password-reset email . Completing a reset invalidates previous sessions and any old private recovery key. Older unverified accounts retain their existing key/provider recovery; email ownership is not used to silently take over or merge an existing account. Keep any private recovery key out of messages and screenshots.
Create notes or checklists, set labels/colors, pin useful items and use search. Save a note before relying on it being persisted. Archives and trash are distinct; permanently deleted content cannot be recovered through the normal UI. Account export and deletion are available.
Write and preview Use standard editing, Markdown preview or split view. Optional Vim uses the editor’s Vim mode; it does not embed a shell or run arbitrary Neovim plugins. A plain-text fallback remains available if the rich editor fails to load.
Formatting, find/replace, in-tab undo/redo and explicit save controls are described in the editor manual . Markdown downloads preserve the note text. Raw HTML and automatically loaded remote images are restricted in preview.
A save failure is not success: keep the draft, read the error and retry. Conflicting revisions require deliberate resolution. In-tab history and dirty-navigation prompts are useful safeguards, not crash-proof or offline storage.
Use Find & commands in the header to search saved titles, passages, checklists and labels. Outside editable fields, Ctrl/Cmd+K opens it; arrows and Enter choose a result, and Escape returns to where you started. Its blank, source and decision templates start an editable draft without replacing existing unsaved work. Keyboard and capture guide .
Add files and manage storage In a note, choose Upload to → Noteweld storage or Google Drive, then attach, paste or drop a supported file into the attachment area. Connect Google Drive separately in Account first. The choice is remembered for your account in this browser; a failed upload never silently changes providers. Images, audio and video use the note’s normal Markdown references. Save the note after insertion. Preview shows supported images and native audio/video players. Browser codec support still applies.
Open Account → Manage storage and plan to see saved-file bytes, unfinished uploads, pending removals and remaining space. The free preview includes 100 MB of managed storage and up to 500 combined managed/Drive attachments; images can be up to 10 MB, audio/video up to 25 MB per file. Archived/trashed notes and unfinished reservations still count.
Expand Manage stored attachments to download or remove a file. Removing an attachment affects every note using it; download a copy first if needed. Removing only its Markdown reference keeps the reusable library file. For notes and actual file bytes together, use Account → Keep a copy → Download Markdown vault. Account JSON remains a separate metadata export.
Plus is planned at $5/month for 5 GB; subscriptions are not available yet. When an account exceeds its current allowance, new uploads pause while existing files, downloads, deletion and note editing remain available. Plan expiry does not automatically delete saved files. Storage and plan details .
Drive originals upload directly from the browser to your connected Google account and use your Google allowance. Noteweld verifies and serves selected media. Removing a Drive reference preserves its original; deleting a managed attachment reclaims its Noteweld storage. Keep the note open to retry an upload. See media/storage choices for retry state, existing-file selection and privacy. A separate owner-operated server profile is available in the source; it is not a third upload destination on this website. See private-server boundaries . Neither deployment offers end-to-end encryption.
Connect the work Insert a stable link using the note picker, or use a title link such as [[Project plan]]. Stable links retain the note’s identity when its title changes. Duplicate titles are ambiguous; missing or unavailable targets are shown explicitly instead of silently choosing another note.
Open a note’s outgoing references and backlinks, or use the graph’s title/label/archive filters and focused neighborhood. The graph also has a keyboard-accessible HTML list. For supported syntax, rename/deletion behavior and all controls, read connections .
Bounds and recovery The free preview is capped at 100 accounts and, per account, 250 notes, 50 labels and 2 MiB of note text. Graph drawing is bounded to 500 nodes/1,000 edges, with at most 256 scanned references per note. These are configured limits, not proof of capacity at every load.
Open a saved note’s History to compare, download or deliberately restore a saved version. Free recovery retains up to ten revisions per note for fourteen days, within 8 MiB of compressed history per account; older versions can expire sooner under pressure. It cannot recreate unsaved text or a deleted media file. A vault export contains current content, not the full history archive. Recovery guide .
There is no paid checkout, collaborative editing or continuous synchronization between browser tabs. Pageweft/Sonaweft ZIP imports have explicit archive/text/traffic limits. Export important work and report unclear behavior to support .
Retain sources and manage sessions Choose Source bundles to preview a supported ZIP, check its categories/hashes and confirm an all-or-nothing import. Original/corrected/AI notes retain their labels; source archives stay separate from edits. Download an original backup. Deleting a retained archive preserves notes but breaks its source-file links. Follow the source guide for limits and duplicate/retry behavior.
For an existing Obsidian or Markdown folder, choose Markdown or Obsidian vault ZIP, inspect the preview and confirm. Configuration and plugins remain inert. Download Markdown vault collects current notes, available stored files and retained sources into an ordinary folder structure with relative links. A missing or disconnected stored file makes collection fail explicitly so you can restore access and retry. Portable vault guide .
In Account, review browser sessions, sign out a session or every device, and confirm recent ownership before sensitive account actions. Google and GitHub are configured. To connect a provider to an existing workspace, sign in to that workspace first, then choose Account → Sessions and connected sign-in → Provider identities and confirm ownership if asked. When the five-minute confirmation expires, choosing a security action takes you to the confirmation field. Enter your current passphrase or select your private recovery key, choose Confirm ownership, then choose the provider action again. Matching emails do not automatically merge accounts. Authorization redirects pass; real owner consent/link acceptance remains pending. Email signup and reset have their separate real inbox acceptance.
Use a local folder or desktop The optional source-distributed CLI connects a local Markdown folder through an explicit browser approval in Account → Devices & agents. Preview a transfer, then confirm that exact preview. Concurrent edits preserve both versions for your decision. Local file deletion never silently deletes the cloud note. Revoking a device stops its further access; already downloaded files remain on that computer. Local-vault sync guide .
The unsigned Linux desktop alpha adds local search, connections, media playback and your actual terminal editor, defaulting to Neovim in a split or expanded pane. Local work needs no account and can be done offline. Cloud sync remains an optional preview/confirmation step. Start with a copy of an important vault. macOS/Windows packages, signing and automatic updates are not qualified, and this is not a public one-click installer. Desktop setup and daily use .
Let an agent prepare work An explicitly paired Agent can read the account’s notes and submit Markdown proposals. It cannot accept its own changes. Open Devices & agents → Review agent proposals, inspect the comparison, then accept or reject. Changed or revoked access refuses stale approvals. The optional DeepTutor MCP bridge uses this same boundary; installing it does not pair an account or change your model. Agent access .
For Anki, the optional CLI previews source-grounded text-card drafts, checks their source hash/quote and exports an import file only after confirmation. Set up the defined note type once and review the import in Anki. Stable IDs let later imports update the same cards while retaining scheduling. This is a text-only handoff; it does not create reviews, run FSRS itself or import into your deck automatically. Anki handoff .
Make the workspace comfortable Open Appearance in the sidebar. Choose Forest, Paper, Slate, Graphite, Ocean or Rose, then light/dark/system mode. The color-group menu exposes 29 independent roles for surfaces/text, controls/feedback, editor/syntax and graph. Light and dark retain separate overrides. Each role has a color picker, hex field and Reset.
Adjust text size, spacing, reading font, reduced motion and stronger borders. Preview changes affect the actual app; choose Save preferences to keep them. Signed-in choices save to your account. Guest appearance saves only in that browser. Note colors and editor keys remain separate.
Use Export/Import theme JSON for a portable copy. Invalid theme files are rejected. Low-contrast choices show a warning; the optional contrast repair changes text colors only when requested. Resetting is a preview until saved. Unsaved account changes prompt before navigation.
Read the interface release for verified behavior and limitations.
title: Using Noteweld

description: Inspect a PDF, choose a conversion method, review the source and keep portable files.
text:
See a completed result Open Pageweft or explore the original PDF/Markdown/ZIP example linked from its website and the portfolio. Viewing the completed example does not run a GPU conversion.
Inspect before processing Upload a PDF you have permission to process. Each file can be at most 64 MiB and 1,000 PDF pages; up to five files can be inspected, with each conversion confirmed separately. Choose the original PDF page numbers or ranges and review the text-layer inspection and quote.
Inspection does not establish that OCR will preserve every formula, table or symbol. Encrypted, malformed or resource-heavy documents can be rejected. Keep the original.
Choose the extraction route Automatic: inspect the per-page text/MinerU routing plan and its quote; keep or deliberately override the conservative heuristic. Forced OCR: request OCR explicitly where the text layer is unsuitable. Text-only: use the cheaper CPU route for available text; it does not provide OCR, extracted images or full layout reconstruction. The small public trial processes one selected page, subject to visitor and shared availability checks. If processing is unavailable, the app displays Currently unavailable. Please try again later. Completed examples remain open. Full funded processing is implemented but unavailable while commercial checkout is closed. Do not assume that seeing a tariff means a live purchase is possible.
Follow work and handle failures Selected pages are divided into bounded sections. Successful sections remain available if another section fails. Inspect the status before retrying; an uncertain request should not be repeated as a new billable job.
Use explicit retry or selected-page reprocessing with its displayed quote. Cancelling queued work and cancelling an already running section have different settlement behavior. The conversion release documents those rules.
Review against the source Use original-PDF page references, reported symptoms and the corrections editor. Corrections remain separate from original engine output; revision checks help prevent stale edits. Detection flags cover specific symptoms and cannot guarantee that unflagged text is correct.
Choose single-document, per-page, page-group or PDF-bookmark exports. The ZIP can carry relative image paths, a manifest, source metadata, original engine output and an optional source PDF. Keep raw output when investigating extraction defects.
Keep your files Download results before the 48-hour retention window expires; scheduled cleanup removes expired source/output files. Saved financial/recovery records are separate from file retention. Use deletion/discard controls when appropriate. Keep any optional private recovery key securely.
Current pricing and boundaries are in the technical overview . Owner deployment and incident procedures are in operations . The owner reports app domains approved; seller/payout and genuine payment acceptance are still required; no earnings or perfect OCR is promised.
Review and portable handoff Compare flagged or edited pages against the original, including printed labels versus PDF indexes. Normalization and cross-page joins offer explicit previews/diffs; saving requires current versions and never rewrites raw engine output. Technical/IPA cues are symptoms, not accuracy certification.
Choose plain Markdown, Obsidian or LLM-oriented exports. Size-targeted chunks preserve Markdown blocks and report oversized ones; they are formatting, not generated summaries. The hashed v1 archive can be previewed and imported atomically through Noteweld sources . See the source-workflow record and quality measurements for actual evidence and remaining representative samples.
Accounts and free availability Use Account to sign in, request an email-first signup link or reset a verified address. Choose the passphrase on the confirmation form; opening the link alone does not create the credential. Existing unverified accounts can verify from their owned workspace. Reset completion signs out older sessions and invalidates old recovery keys. A separately saved key is optional when verified email recovery is available. Matching addresses never merge accounts; confirming signup in another browser creates a fresh workspace rather than moving guest files/credits. Google/GitHub registration and genuine consent acceptance remain separate. Email and recovery guide . Signing in does not grant another sample or reset limits. Shared availability is checked privately; owner billing/accounting details are not returned to visitors.
title: Using Pageweft

description: Go from an authorized recording to a timestamped transcript and portable source-linked notes.
text:
Hear a completed example Open the completed scientific example to hear a human-voiced NOAA interview about gravity, follow actual recognition text and download a hashed bundle. Prepared listening notes are labeled separately from optional review-provider output. This precomputed example does not start another transcription job.
Upload and inspect The hosted workflow accepts authorized English audio/video up to 64 MiB and 60 minutes. Upload a file and inspect its duration/quote before confirming work. The hosted application does not download arbitrary platform URLs or use your browser cookies.
An available free sample processes the first 30 seconds, transcription only. It is once per workspace/IP hash and subject to small global and admission quotas. The owner reports app domains approved; paid packs stay closed until seller/payout and genuine payment acceptance pass.
Decide whether to use AI review Review is optional and requires consent to send transcript text to DeepSeek. Source audio is not sent to that text provider. Standard/advanced review choices have different quoted service tariffs; current values are in the technical overview .
Original recognition, user corrections, generated notes and separately sourced research remain different artifacts. A generated summary or scholarly metadata match does not certify that a claim is true.
Listen, correct and export Open timestamped segments, listen to the corresponding source and search the text. Save corrections as a separate revision; the original recognition remains available. Conflicts or failed saves need resolution before you rely on the edit.
Export original Markdown/text/JSON/SRT/VTT, corrected Markdown/JSON and optional notes/research questions. The versioned instascript-export/v1 bundle includes identity, timing, provenance and hashes. You can preview/import that bundle through Noteweld sources , preserving original/corrected/AI labels and retained files within its bounds.
Failed selected processing releases its reservation; an explicit retry gets a fresh quote and may reuse retained recognition. Do not blindly create a second job after an uncertain response.
Local CLI and retention The standalone CLI also supports authorized URLs through its own local tools. Local model downloads, platform access and optional provider charges are separate from the hosted service. Follow the CLI setup , not the archived agent/demo scripts.
Hosted source/results expire after 48 hours and are removed by scheduled cleanup. Download outputs while retained. Use the immediate source/result delete controls to close access, return active holds and remove files; bounded in-flight processing buffers expire when their operation exits. Financial records remain separate. Manual speaker labels are annotations; automatic diarization, verified speaker identity and certified transcription are not claimed.
Direct sources and source review The hosted importer accepts authorized public HTTPS direct media or RSS/Atom feeds with bounded, checked redirects. It does not download arbitrary webpages/YouTube, access private feeds or use browser cookies. Inspect before confirming. Selected-time-span quotes create a separate result with its original recording offset; earlier results and edits remain.
Use playback speed/selection loop, source-linked quotes, listening cues and glossary candidates to review uncertain material. These are transparent symptoms, not calibrated truth scores. Optional AI suggestions can be staged/dismissed deliberately and saved as user corrections; original ASR stays unchanged. Read the source-workflow release for controls, deletion and diagnostic boundaries.
Accounts and free availability Use Account to sign in, request an email-first signup link or reset a verified address. Choose the passphrase on the confirmation form; opening the link alone does not create the credential. Existing unverified accounts can verify from their owned workspace. Reset completion signs out older sessions and invalidates old recovery keys. A separately saved key is optional when verified email recovery is available. Matching addresses never merge accounts; confirming signup in another browser creates a fresh workspace rather than moving guest files/credits. Google/GitHub registration and genuine consent acceptance remain separate. Email and recovery guide . Signing in does not reset sample eligibility. If processing is unavailable, the app displays Currently unavailable. Please try again later. Completed examples remain open and owner billing/accounting stays private.
The scientific example record explains the source, credit and what the saved transcript demonstrates.
title: Using Sonaweft

description: Understand the separate browser-only demonstration and its storage boundary.
text:
Open the portfolio demo Open the bundled demo or launch it from the portfolio’s vanilla JavaScript card. This is a separate implementation from Noteweld. It demonstrates native browser APIs rather than the professional Next.js application.
Work in one browser Try notes and checklists, pin/color/label controls, archive and trash. Storage belongs to this browser and website origin. It does not create a cloud account, synchronize devices or inherit Noteweld’s editor/graph features.
Use a disposable test note when exploring the demo. Browser data clearing, private browsing, storage limits or a different origin can affect persistence. Keep important content outside a portfolio demonstration.
Save, search and recover Use either search field to find titles, bodies, labels or checklist text. Create a text note or checklist; labels imported in a JSON backup are available in navigation immediately. Use the edit button or open a card; Escape saves and returns focus.
Export a JSON backup before clearing browser storage. Imports validate the file and merge without replacing existing note IDs. When a save fails, the app shows an error and retains an open draft for retry. Malformed existing data opens a recovery screen with a raw JSON download instead of reseeding the database.
Archive keeps a note available for later. Delete from Archive moves it to Trash. Restore recovers it; Delete forever and Empty Trash ask for confirmation. There is no automatic seven-day deletion.
Release boundary The published portfolio bundle is refreshed from the same production build as the standalone demo. The source release records 14 unit tests, 22 Chromium journeys, four viewport widths and no automated WCAG A/AA findings on the tested seeded screens. These checks do not certify every browser or replace usability testing.
Reminders and inactive settings controls are omitted. The professional Noteweld editor, Vim mode, graph, cloud accounts and payments are separate. Read the implementation guide and release history for the exact boundary.
title: Using the vanilla demo

description: NixOS, Home Manager, Hyprland and the boundaries between reproducible packages and personal state.
text:
Start with the source NixOS configuration repository · Published Neovim configuration The public NixOS repository is the published baseline. The local security maintenance verified on 16 October has not yet been committed to that repository. The interactive guide uses short, explanatory examples; it is not a copy of private machine state.
Two configuration layers The flake pins Nixpkgs, Home Manager and Fenix. NixOS declares system packages, hardware integration and services. Home Manager declares user packages and configuration links. The system build integrates both layers, so package/configuration changes can be reviewed together.
flake.lock records exact input revisions. A pinned build still needs compatible hardware, application data and separately restored credentials.
A keyboard-first desktop Hyprland runs the Wayland desktop, with XWayland available for applications that need it. SDDM handles login; Kitty provides the terminal, Waybar the status bar, and Rofi the launcher. PipeWire and WirePlumber provide audio and media routing.
Configured desktop shortcuts include Super + Return for the terminal, Super + B for the browser, Super + Space for the launcher and Super + O for file search. These are configuration examples rather than browser shortcuts.
Intel graphics drive the laptop display. NVIDIA is available through explicit offload. This separation keeps ordinary desktop work on the integrated GPU while allowing a compatible task to request the dedicated GPU.
Packages and mutable state Nix supplies Neovim and its language servers. Personal Lua configuration comes from a separate live Neovim checkout. Application data, working trees, browser profiles, credentials and databases are separate state; they are not recreated by a package build.
Secrets belong outside public source and outside unfiltered flake sources. Git ignoring a file does not protect it from every other tool that copies a directory.
What was actually checked On 16 October, the prepared security configuration passed a full NixOS build and was activated successfully. Both Home Manager activations succeeded. System DNS resolved a real domain, NVIDIA-offloaded OpenGL reported the MX350 renderer, and Hyprland reported no configuration errors. Both storage drives passed fresh short self-tests. These are dated observations, not a guarantee about every future workload.
Read build and verification for the maintenance sequence and remaining boundaries, or return to the interactive Workbench .
title: How the environment fits together

description: CPU web hosting, on-demand workers and the costs that remain after compute stops.
text:
More than a GPU rental Modal runs application containers on CPU as well as GPU resources. It supports HTTP applications, background functions, schedules, persistent volumes and secrets. An HTTP server can be Python/FastAPI or a Node process; the deployment wrapper does not require every application to be written in Python.
Official references: HTTP applications , autoscaling , persistent volumes and secrets . Checked on 16 October 2026; provider policies and prices can change.
The current deployment Component Hosting Persistent state Portfolio, vanilla demo and this Hugo library GitHub Pages Static versioned files; vanilla demo uses browser storage Pageweft web/API and extraction jobs Modal CPU containers and A10G workers Separate document and serialized SQLite ledger volumes Sonaweft web/API, speech and review coordination Modal CPU containers and L4 workers Separate media, model-cache and serialized SQLite ledger volumes Noteweld web/API Modal Node/Next.js CPU container Isolated Neon PostgreSQL; encrypted backups in Modal Paddle handles commercial payments rather than hosting these websites. DeepSeek is an optional text-inference provider for Sonaweft. No shared customer wallet or login is implemented. Linguavell is a separate startup project.
Why this choice fits the previews Pageweft already had working MinerU execution on Modal. Reusing that provider allowed a small CPU web process to dispatch bounded expensive extraction separately. Sonaweft fits the same pattern with speech workers. Noteweld can run as a standard Node server, retaining portable PostgreSQL access rather than requiring another web-host account.
Containers can shut down after inactivity. The laptop is only a development/deployment client and does not need to remain online for the hosted applications to work. The Hugo blog is static and adds no application server or paid API.
The tradeoffs A request after inactivity can wait for a cold start. Keeping containers warm improves responsiveness but increases cost. Retained files, cached models, scheduled cleanup, database storage, backups and network usage can still consume resources when no customer job runs. Scale-to-zero compute is not a universal zero-bill promise.
Current container/concurrency caps deliberately constrain the previews. They are not a measured promise for thousands of simultaneous users. Internal admission allowances are distinct from a provider-wide spending limit. External automatic alerts and a saved global hard spending cap are not established by these releases.
Portability and review Noteweld uses a Node application and standard PostgreSQL driver; it can move to another suitable container/PostgreSQL host with configuration and deployment work. The Python applications keep processing logic separate from Modal wrappers, but function dispatch, volumes and scheduling are real provider dependencies. Migration would require replacing those integrations and validating storage/ledger semantics.
The current arrangement is an economical starting point to measure. Actual invoices, customer workload and cold-start tolerance should guide later hosting changes. It does not establish that Modal will be the cheapest host at every future traffic level.
title: Why these previews run on Modal

description: The actual configured editing workflow: Telescope, Harpoon, language servers, formatting and Markdown.
text:
Follow a small loop Find a file, make a focused change, inspect diagnostics, format it, and run the relevant check. The editor shortens that loop; it does not establish that a change is correct.
The configured leader is Space. These mappings come from the published Neovim source , inspected alongside the local checkout.
Action Configured mapping Tool Find project files Space, s, f Telescope Search file contents Space, s, g Telescope live grep Remember a working file Space, a Harpoon Open the remembered-file menu Ctrl + e Harpoon Format a buffer Space, f Conform Move between editor splits Ctrl + h / j / k / l Neovim window navigation Language support through Nix The Neovim wrapper supplies language-server and formatter executables: gopls, TypeScript language server, nil, Pyright, clangd, Lua language server, Marksman and rust-analyzer among them. Formatting tools include Stylua, nixfmt, gofumpt, Black and Ruff.
This avoids depending on ordinary Linux binary downloads that may assume filesystem paths unavailable on NixOS. Plugin configuration and language-server behavior still need testing for the particular project.
Code and technical writing The setup includes Treesitter grammars, Telescope, Harpoon, Conform and Markdown-oriented tooling. It supports moving between source code and technical notes while keeping tools close to the current buffer.
The Workbench’s browser editor demonstrates a deliberately small subset: h/j/k/l movement, i for insert, Escape for normal mode, x for deletion and u for undo. File switching retains each temporary buffer within the page. It is an interactive keyboard sketch of the workflow, with native browser controls available throughout.
Verification boundary An actual headless Neovim startup succeeded on 16 October, and twelve selected language-server/formatter executables resolved inside its wrapped environment. That check does not certify every plugin, language server or debugger. The next deeper check is a representative edit/diagnostic/format/test journey for each language actually used on a client project.
Current display behavior The later Neovim display repair restored shared JavaScript/JSX Tree-sitter queries and distinct syntax groups. Mathematical operator substitutions are opt-in, and diagnostics use signs/floats/lists instead of inserting long messages into source lines. These were exercised with 62 editor checks on 5 November; that evidence is specific to the repaired workflow.
The Workbench remains a browser-only keyboard sketch. It does not run the native editor or certify every plugin, parser or language server.
title: Neovim: find, edit, inspect

description: The implementation sequence, successful commands, deployment prerequisites and recorded corrections.
text:
Start from the evidence The current source is connected-notes handoff f6901ff (owner-access source record). Application code for that collection is e1b8740; earlier foundations are not descriptions of every current feature. Read the usage guide before following the implementation record.
1. Repair account and note persistence The early registration work validated identity/password input, seeded accounts and preserved failed form input. The then-selected Neon HTTP adapter supported a batch operation rather than interactive transaction callbacks. Its mocked-transport checks were explicitly not evidence of database rollback.
The reliability foundation switched to standard pg/Drizzle transactions shared between local PostgreSQL and Neon. It added real seed rollback/races, per-account ownership, note revisions/idempotency, trash rules and label consistency. A new database and restricted runtime role were provisioned for the preview; the original Keep database was not migrated. The private provisioning values are deliberately absent from this library.
Recovery-key hashing, session revocation, export/deletion, bounded signup/storage, CSP and encrypted backups followed. Foundation code 4d79e53 passed actual source CI (run 38801749405; owner-access source record). The original eight hosted browser journeys passed; a nonempty hosted snapshot was restored into an isolated local clone.
2. Add the editor without losing failure recovery Code cbd60fe added CodeMirror Markdown, safe preview/split, optional Vim, save shortcuts, exact Markdown downloads and dirty-navigation guards. The public example used the actual editor without an account or upload. Narrow split panes were stacked after phone review. Failed saves, expired sessions and a deliberately failed editor load were exercised; the plain editor fallback remained usable.
The collection passed 33 unit/React, 13 real PostgreSQL and 11 hosted browser checks. Editor record .
3. Connect notes by identity Code e1b8740 added stable ID links, explicit title ambiguity/missing states, linked-note pages, outgoing/backlink views and bounded graph navigation. A shared Markdown-aware scanner excluded code/HTML/existing links. Public example notes used no private API. Graph fitting and constant screen-size labels were corrected during visual review.
The collection passed 40 unit/React, 14 PostgreSQL and 14 hosted browser checks. Connected release and successful CI (run 38877398787; owner-access source record).
Successful check commands These are the repository’s actual release entrypoints. Database/browser commands need the isolated local PostgreSQL configuration described in the repository; never substitute an old production database URL.
npm ci npm run lint npm test npm run test:database npm run typecheck npm run build npm run test:browser Installed Next.js documentation was read before relevant API/component changes. Modal deployment uses the reviewed source allowlist, pinned Node image, existing noteweld-runtime secret and isolated Neon role. The owner used a private staged source directory to exclude credentials. The deploy entrypoint is:
python -m modal deploy app.py That command requires an authenticated Modal SDK environment and the established private runtime configuration. It does not create or approve accounts. Health is /api/health; encrypted snapshot/restore and incident steps are in operations .
Recorded failures and corrections Finding Correction and acceptance Early HTTP driver could not provide interactive transaction callbacks Use standard PostgreSQL driver; test actual rollback, duplicate races and ownership on disposable databases Original runtime dependencies had known advisories Compatible Next/sharp/source-map-js patches; rerun build, database/browser checks and runtime audit Narrow split editor and graph labels were difficult to read Stack panes and fit the visible graph while retaining readable screen-size labels; inspect phone screenshots Save conflict or failed network could lose confidence in a draft Preserve the draft and expose conflict/retry; exercise deliberate failures and recovery in the real browser Development-only upstream advisories remain documented. In-tab history is not a durable revision archive. Pageweft/Sonaweft bundle imports and commercial checkout were not implemented by these releases.
title: Building Noteweld: accounts to connected notes

description: From a Modal MinerU worker to source-aware exports, credit accounting and payment readiness.
text:
1. Establish actual extraction The initial requirement was private PDF-to-Markdown preparation using MinerU on the owner’s Modal account. The design moved from customer-provided Modal credentials to owner-hosted processing; customers do not provide cloud tokens. MinerU 2.7.6 runs in a cloud GPU image and retains original engine output. The laptop’s 2 GB GPU is not required.
A bounded one-page public trial was verified before describing full-book processing. The initial deployed web startup failed because modal_fn.py was missing from its uploaded source. Explicit inclusion fixed the image, followed by a fresh deployment and public workflow checks. Original verification record .
2. Make books and partial failure manageable Book inspection/ranges, explicit quotes, 20-page sections, partial outputs, selected retries, force OCR, cheaper CPU text extraction and cancellation were implemented. Source page indices were mapped back to the original PDF. Corrections/revision checks remained separate from engine output; exports preserved relative images, manifests, bookmarks and optional source PDF.
Actual GPU extraction checked selected pages from an original four-page fixture. A separate complete 1,000-page synthetic PDF passed the CPU text route across 50 sections with ordered pages and correct fixture-credit settlement. This proves that workflow on those sources; it does not prove scanned-book fidelity. Book release .
3. Account for usage and recovery The book ledger has one serialized writer, distinct from the older prototype ledger. Credit holds are reserved, settled or released transactionally; duplicate confirmation does not dispatch twice. Processing and file retention are separate from persistent financial records. Owner reports, admission envelopes, pause and encrypted snapshots were added. Admission estimates are not a whole-account cloud bill cap.
One-time $5/$10 packs replaced the earlier monthly access proposal. Rename commit 1372062 introduced Pageweft while retaining cloud/storage identities. Paddle integration commit e7a70ee (owner-access source record) superseded the Lemon Squeezy activation path. Signed events enter a durable inbox; fresh provider state and server-owned intents control grants/refunds. Current source has 78 automated checks; payment HTTP in those checks is mocked.
Successful commands and prerequisites The established owner deployment uses Python 3.13, authenticated Modal SDK 1.5.3, existing permanent session/payment secrets and separate ledger/results/model volumes. GPU dependencies run in the cloud image.
python3.13 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -q node --check static/app.js .venv/bin/python -m modal deploy app.py For the recorded local browser fixture, with explicitly synthetic funds and real CPU text extraction:
.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn scripts.preview_books:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8768 Owner verification uses scripts.probe_deployed_books with an authorized original fixture and an explicit --mode text or --mode auto. Those probes seed internal verification credit; they are not purchases. scripts/test_e2e.py targets an older interface and is not the active release test.
Owner commands which were actually used for operations include:
.venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations report .venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations backup Reports/backups remain private. Never publish a source book, recovery key, provider credential or decrypted ledger while reproducing them.

Interpret evidence precisely Static checks establish particular code/build properties. Unit tests can substitute model, network or authentication boundaries. Database tests establish behavior on an actual disposable database. Browser journeys exercise visible flows and selected failure cases. description: A practical maintenance sequence that keeps source review, builds, activation and real runtime evidence distinct.
text:
Review before changing the system Inspect Git state and the relevant diff. Back up files being changed privately. Preserve unrelated work, the current lock file and a known working boot generation. New files referenced by a Git-backed flake must be deliberately included in its source.
Use a Git-filtered flake source. An explicit unfiltered path: source may include ignored private files before a build-time check can reject them.
Match the check to the change Change Relevant evidence Documentation Generated pages, links, keyboard and browser checks User-profile application Package build, executable, launch and a real file operation NixOS service Option evaluation, system build, activation and actual service behavior Graphics/kernel update Supported hardware branch, complete build, rollback route and controlled boot acceptance Backup procedure Retained-data fixtures, successful real copy and a separate restore test For this machine, the nr shortcut runs sudo nixos-rebuild switch against the NixOS flake. It does not decrypt secrets, stage files or commit changes. Administrative authentication remains an operating-system boundary.
The verified maintenance example The 16 October security pass enabled the stateful firewall, restricted local DNS, separated root’s editor from mutable personal Lua, removed the global browser decoder-sandbox override, and removed unattended Git publication. The non-deleting HDD copy was repaired and actually completed. Syncthing received HDD mount guards and private-file exclusions; Unicode filename conflicts were corrected while preserving both original byte copies.

Recovery remains explicit The same-machine HDD copies and legacy Borg repository are not an independent encrypted recovery plan. Credential recovery, backup encryption and a controlled system/driver upgrade remain separate work. Existing browser processes inherit their startup environment until restarted. An offline paired phone prevents an end-to-end sync observation even when local checks pass.
The original public configuration predates this local maintenance pass. Publishing a reviewed source revision is a separate step; the guides do not represent the baseline repository as already containing unpublished changes.

description: A concrete Sonaweft improvement, from a code map to transaction tests, accessible comparison and portable recovery.
text:
The user problem A transcript can be corrected successfully while the editing workflow still loses valuable work. In-tab undo is insufficient after a reload, and a revision number prevents conflicting saves without keeping the earlier text. Sonaweft now keeps bounded, durable annotation snapshots and lets the owner compare and restore them. The original recognition remains a separate source throughout.
Try the live workbench or read the history usage guide . A completed original example is readable without consuming processing credit.
Find the boundaries before changing the interface A local Graphify code-only map of the relevant source snapshot contained 512 nodes and 1,442 relationships. It directed review toward the annotation writer, source deletion, expiry cleanup, exports and financial snapshots. The graph was a navigation aid; source inspection and executed tests established the behavior.
That review found an existing privacy defect: deleting a recording cleared correction text but left its current speaker-label fields in the ledger. The repair clears both, removes history immediately and excludes annotation content from financial snapshots. Retention cannot be implemented solely as a visible history dropdown.
Make recovery atomic The existing serialized SQLite writer now saves an annotation and its history in one transaction. Snapshot failure rolls back the annotation. Every restore checks ownership, result expiry, CSRF, request rate and the expected current revision. Concurrent restores/saves cannot both overwrite the same revision.
The latest 20 states are retained per result. Restoring an older one creates a new revision rather than rewriting its predecessor. Existing results begin with their actual saved state; missing historical timestamps are not invented.
Keep the interaction explicit The comparison uses inert text and shows changes across the whole result. Previewing it does not modify the editor. Unsaved correction and speaker-label drafts prevent restore; a confirmation explains its full-result scope. Fields are temporarily locked while an annotation write is in flight, and stale reads cannot repopulate a different result. Refreshing read-only listening cues also preserves unsaved correction and speaker-label drafts. Malformed Unicode labels are rejected without a partial save.
Browser testing also exposed a missing return path from interval quoting. Use the full recording now re-quotes the same upload without duplicating media or starting inference. It does not reset a consumed free allowance.
On phones, controls stack naturally. Motion respects reduced-motion preferences; entry animation is limited to the review heading, avoiding a large composited editor layer. Functional layout and accessibility belong with the feature, before the separate final visual-polish pass.
Check real boundaries 90 backend checks passed, including real SQLite reopen, concurrency, rollback, retention, ownership, deletion, legacy revision preservation and backup exclusion. DOM checks covered inert text, draft safety, failed-read retry, failed restore, stale responses and explicit server-priced quoting without starting processing. Real Chromium exercised local SQLite, actual media inspection/decoding and an explicitly replayed original ASR fixture: edit, label, compare, restore, reload, export and delete at 320/390/768/1440 widths. The review panel had no automated WCAG A/AA findings. This is not physical-device, Safari or human usability evidence. The exported history is hashed in the manifest. The actual Noteweld validator accepted the ZIP as two notes and fourteen retained files, including the history. Before deployment, an encrypted financial snapshot passed an isolated integrity and balance check. Public HTML/JavaScript/CSS matched the deployed release bytes; the new history endpoint rejected anonymous access and billing stayed closed. During testing, reusing a local preview exhausted its real global trial quota. The correct fix was a fresh isolated preview ledger, not a larger production allowance. A stale status-text expectation was corrected too.
A Strix experiment did not produce a completed security assessment: its default example model was unavailable on the subscription, and a compatible-model run was stopped for excessive context overhead before finishing. It is not recorded as a clean pentest. Targeted source review and executed security tests remain the evidence for this release; broader testing is a separate controlled task.
What this adds commercially Basic editing and export are established features: Mathpix documents editable PDF conversion and export , and Descript describes text-based media editing . Sources checked 19 October 2026. A history dropdown alone is not a defensible moat.
The product hypothesis is a useful combination: source-linked review, recoverable edits, explicit processing costs and portable outputs that keep working in the user’s own tools. Its commercial advantage must be measured in correction time, successful exports, return usage and willingness to pay. These engineering checks do not establish market demand, superior recognition accuracy or profitability.
For a client, the case study exposes concrete delivery work: finding a privacy defect, protecting state under failure, implementing a usable recovery flow and verifying it across the API, database, browser and exported files.

description: LocalStorage behavior, setup, backup/import design and known release work.
text:
A free, browser-only notes and checklist demo built with native DOM APIs, CSS, localStorage and Webpack. It shares Noteweld’s product family and deliberately has no account, server or paid features. The existing Keep repository and public URL are preserved.
Live demo · Source · Portfolio and manuals Features Create and edit notes and checklists; pin, color, label, archive, trash and restore them. Search titles, bodies, labels and checklist text from either search control. Use keyboard navigation, named controls and a focus-contained edit dialog; Escape saves and returns focus. Export versioned JSON including archived/trashed notes and labels; validate and merge imports without replacing existing IDs. Preserve drafts when a storage write fails, display an error and allow retry. Recover raw stored JSON if existing notes are malformed, without silently resetting user data. Use a responsive layout with readable colored notes and reduced-motion support. Delete from Archive moves to recoverable Trash. Delete forever and Empty Trash require confirmation. There is no automatic seven-day purge. Header Refresh reloads this browser view; the layout control switches compact display. Placeholder reminders/settings are omitted from the available controls.
Run and verify Use Node.js 24. Development serves only on loopback.
npm ci npm run dev # Open http://localhost:3000 npm test npm run build npx playwright install chromium npm run test:e2e npm audit On NixOS, use an installed compatible Chromium via PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/run/current-system/sw/bin/chromium. The lockfile pins tested dependencies. A small loopback-only Node server serves the generated demo; Webpack watches source changes, and you refresh the page to see them. It has no proxy, uploads or hot-reload service. Unit tests cover storage, backup validation/rollback and checklist editing. Browser tests exercise persistence, import/export, keyboard controls, failed saves, corrupt-data recovery and four viewport widths. Automated accessibility checks supplement keyboard and visual review; they do not certify every possible user journey.
The Pages workflow builds dist/ from source. The portfolio embeds a copy of that production bundle; a release must update both and verify public pages.
Code map src/index.js: boot, recovery and shared DOM helpers. src/header/, src/side/: search and keyboard navigation. src/main/notes/notes-store.js: persisted notes and labels. src/main/notes/backup.js: validated, additive JSON portability. src/main/notes/checklist-editor.js: checklist UI. src/main/notes/notes.js: composer, edit dialog, cards and filters. src/main/notes/storage-feedback.js: visible persistence failures. src/main/archive/, src/main/trash/: recovery and explicit deletion. tests/: unit and browser acceptance cases. Different sites/origins have separate storage, while the portfolio and its embedded demo share an origin; avoid putting sensitive material in a showcase.
The package declares ISC; no standalone license file was present in the original repository. This release does not invent an MIT grant or change asset ownership. description: Design rationale and evaluation criteria; the usage guide describes current availability.
text:
Implementation update The approved core features are now implemented: full-book/range inspection (bounded at 64 MiB/1,000 pages), batch inspection, quotes, bounded section processing, selective retries/force OCR, source-linked review, corrections/history, portable outputs and prepaid-credit accounting. Read BOOK-RELEASE.md for tested evidence and limits. Earlier candidate language below describes the design rationale. Actual merchant activation and comparative difficult-document fidelity remain unverified; these features do not certify every source symbol.
Pageweft: conversion utility User clarification, 14 October 2026: PDF-to-Markdown for serious work with books, including Linguavell preparation. Users control the downstream reading/LLM workflow. No study platform, AI chat, automatically generated teaching materials or decorative feature expansion.
Product hypothesis Turn difficult books and technical PDFs into portable, source-traceable Markdown with less manual repair and predictable processing costs. Modal is infrastructure; MinerU is a selected engine. Customers buy the result and saved setup/repair time, not the provider combination.
Strongest initial cohort: repeated book/PDF conversion users who want plain files for their own editor, scripts or LLM. Students/scientists are qualified by this concrete need, not by profession or document volume alone. An occasional converter may reasonably reject a monthly subscription; validate actual return usage rather than assuming continuing demand.
Existing verified foundation Owner-hosted pinned MinerU 2.7.6 with private CLI worker; no customer Modal credentials. One-selected-page bounded public trial after book inspection; per-session/IP quotas and global admission controls. These are not a provider-wide invoice limit. Persistent serialized job/quota ledger, duplicate-request suppression and session-owned downloads. Markdown/images, original PDF, available source block/page metadata and navigation, detectable replacement glyph and missing-image report. Real public synthetic PDF upload → conversion → ZIP download passed. This does not establish book fidelity, rendered Markdown compatibility across editors, medical accuracy or complete coverage for every PDF page. Current pricing uses one-time $5/$10 processing packs without recurring access fees; transactional credit accounting is implemented. Actual seller activation and payment delivery remain unverified. The former monthly access model is superseded. Original design rationale (core now implemented; evidence in BOOK-RELEASE.md) Book handling: accept suitably bounded full books; allow selected PDF pages/ranges; split work into bounded sections; join output without losing images or order; preserve original PDF page references. Retries must rerun only failed selected work. The current public trial and disabled 50-page paid draft do not satisfy this requirement. Fidelity: evaluate reading order, headings, paragraphs, hyphenation, footnotes, tables, formulas and specialized Unicode/IPA against rendered source pages. Flag detectable defects separately from unchecked correctness; do not silently guess or paraphrase the source. Portable files: standard Markdown plus documented extensions when needed, relative local image paths, one-document or section exports, optional PDF-page links. Reprocessing must not change unaffected filenames or introduce duplicate pages. Keep raw engine output separate from optional normalization. Review and repair: show reported defects and the relevant source page; preserve the user’s edits. Allow selected-page re-extraction with visible price and changes. No promise of automatic perfect error detection or universally accurate OCR. Predictable cost: show a bounded quote before confirmation; reserve processing funds transactionally; settle measured/defined tariff costs; release unused funds; handle failed jobs according to disclosed rules; prevent duplicate debits/dispatch. Subscription access and compute balance are separate gates. Cost-aware extraction: evaluate reliable text-layer extraction before spending GPU time, then OCR where justified. Must demonstrate preserved structure/symbols on the benchmark before becoming a default. Using a cheaper route is not itself a quality improvement. Engine alternatives are benchmark candidates, not automatic new dependencies or migrations. These are proposed improvements consistent with the user’s direction, not approved novelty claims or completed features. Each must justify saved setup or correction time. Integration means portable outputs usable in the user’s own tools; it does not require proprietary Obsidian/AI plugins.
Benchmark before differentiation claims Use permission-cleared documents covering a clean digital textbook, scanned/older print, multi-column paper, mathematical tables/formulas, phonetic symbols and long-book section boundaries. Keep private source books private; use original synthetic/openly licensed samples for public demonstrations and third-party uploads only where permitted.
For each: exact engine/version/options; selected pages; byte/page counts; output integrity; missing/duplicated sections; significant symbol/numeric errors; broken image references; reading-order failures; human correction minutes per sampled page; elapsed time and actual billed cost. Errors without U+FFFD remain possible. A source-map page count is not proof that all source content survived.
Compare the same documents/tasks with native MinerU output and appropriate existing converters. Provider capability descriptions establish candidate baselines, not local victories. Choose differentiation only when observed: lower total cleanup time, less setup, clearer price, or a better supported difficult-document profile. No need to invent a feature that no other tool has; measurable utility is the commercial test.
Commercial experiment: 20 qualified testers, at least 5 actual paying users and 3 second-month returns are initial decision checkpoints, not market-size estimates. Keep larger development/paid acquisition proportional to evidence. At $1/month, assess net contribution and owner support time; popularity alone is insufficient.
title: Conversion product design

description: Editing modes, keyboard controls, safe previews, exports and draft boundaries.
text:
Open a text note or choose Take a note…. Checklists keep their separate checklist editor.
Write, Preview and Split change the view without discarding source or enhanced-editor undo. Split stacks vertically on narrow screens. Standard keys work by default. Vim enables normal/insert/visual modes, motions, selection and Vim undo. Use i to insert, Escape to return to normal, v to select and u to undo. Escape in Vim stays inside the note. Simple text provides a native textarea for accessibility, device compatibility or enhanced-editor loading failure. Switching to/from it starts fresh enhanced-editor undo; source is retained. Settings apply to this editing session. Undo, Redo, Find and the formatting buttons work in the enhanced editor. Find includes replacement. Tab leaves the editor instead of trapping keyboard focus. Save or Ctrl/Cmd-S writes through the normal API. Vim :w uses the same path. Existing notes stay open after these saves; Save & close also closes. Saving a new note completes its creation. Escape/backdrop closure asks before discarding an edited note; it does not silently save it. A failed save leaves the draft and undo available. If another tab changed the note, copy or download the draft before Reload saved version. Reloading is a deliberate replacement and clears the old draft’s undo history. There is no durable server revision archive yet. Download .md exports the exact current body, including unsaved changes, with the title as a portable filename. It does not insert a heading or modify stored data. Account JSON export still includes all notes and labels. Media attachments — 6 November In a signed-in note, use Attach media or drop/paste a file. Preview displays owned images, audio and video; Manage attachments reuses or removes account files. Checklists expose the same body under Attachments and details. Free accounts have 100 MB storage, 10 MB images and 25 MB audio/video files. Removing one file makes its references unavailable wherever used. Markdown/JSON exports contain references/metadata; download original media separately. See the media manual and hosted evidence .
Privacy and limits Markdown rendering, syntax and Vim run in the browser. No AI request, external font or paid processing provider is added. Preview supports CommonMark and GFM tables/task lists. Raw HTML is ignored. Only explicit HTTP(S), mail and fragment links are clickable; application-relative and script/data/file links are disabled. External links open separately without a referrer. Verified owned media and source-figure URLs render through authenticated application requests. Arbitrary external images display descriptions and optional links without automatic requests.
Source text remains in the existing note body; the editor itself needs no migration. Media metadata uses additive migration 0010. The enhanced editor preserves whitespace and mixed line separators by using explicit LF splitting. Its 100,000 UTF-16-unit limit matches the existing API boundary. An oversized paste is rejected whole, with a visible message, rather than silently truncated. Account-wide quotas and request limits still apply.
Drafts and undo exist only in the open tab. Save before navigating, and keep downloads/backups for important material. A tab-close warning is not crash recovery. Neither content nor editor preferences are copied into localStorage. This is not end-to-end encryption.
Public example /example uses the same editor with original demonstration text. It needs no account and sends no scratchpad to an API. Its Ctrl/Cmd-S and Vim :w download Markdown. Reset and ordinary navigation warn before discarding changed content. This is a scratchpad demonstration, not simulated cloud persistence.
Implementation MarkdownEditor owns views, fallback, status and download; CodeEditor owns one CodeMirror instance with replaceable key/read-only compartments. Callbacks route through the current component state; the global Vim Ex command routes through a WeakMap keyed by actual editor instance. Component cleanup destroys the view and removes its save handler. Switching views/keys retains history; a deliberate saved-version reload remounts it.
Both enhanced editing and Markdown preview load in separate client chunks. A failed editor chunk falls back to the controlled native textarea, preserving text. A failed preview chunk leaves Write available. The dependency set is pinned in the lockfile; CodeMirror, its Vim adapter, react-markdown and remark-gfm are MIT licensed. No raw-HTML plugin or weakened script CSP is used.
Primary references: CodeMirror state/view documentation , official Vim adapter , react-markdown security , remark-gfm . Installed Next 16.3.8 client/lazy-loading guides were read for this implementation.
Automated browser evidence is Chromium on Linux. Physical mobile keyboards, IME composition, screen readers and Safari/Firefox remain separate compatibility checks; the native textarea is available without pretending those devices have been certified.

description: Stable note identities, title resolution, graph controls and connection limits.
text:
Choose Link note while writing to insert a stable reference such as [[note:UUID|Readable caption]]. Search titles/labels, select a note and insert; the editor keeps your cursor position and undo. Escape closes the picker and returns focus. A stable ID survives a rename; its optional caption remains the text you wrote, while the link tooltip shows the current title. Copy a stable reference from any note’s detail page too.
You can also type [[Title]] or [[Title|caption]]. Matching uses trimmed, case-folded NFKC titles across your own active and archived notes. Exactly one match resolves. Duplicate titles show ambiguous; missing titles show unavailable. These are name lookups, not permanent identity: use the picker for links that must survive renames or replacement by another note with the same title. Empty titles cannot be looked up by name; link them by ID. No note is created or rewritten automatically.
Wiki references must fit on one line, with at most 200 characters in each target/caption. Escape brackets, pipes or backslashes with a backslash; the picker does this. Code blocks, inline code, raw HTML and existing Markdown links/images (including GFM autolinks) are excluded. Syntax scanning is shared by the preview, metadata, backlinks and graph. The first 256 valid references in a note participate; a visible notice explains when more remain literal source. Downloads/account exports retain the full source.
Reading and backlinks Internal preview links open /dashboard/note/ID. These authenticated detail pages show full Markdown or a checklist, note controls, copyable stable references, outgoing links and saved backlinks. Archived notes still work. Trash is excluded from the connection index; a trashed reference becomes unavailable and works again after restoration. Permanent deletion never retargets a stable reference, including when another note gets the same title. Guessed IDs from another account return a generic not-found result.
In an open note, expand Links and backlinks. Outgoing references use the current draft, while backlinks come from saved notes. Repeated references from the same source do not create extra backlinks. Existing labels serve as tags and graph filters. They retain their current ownership, rename and deletion behavior.
Connections refresh after confirmed writes in the same workspace. Use Refresh connections, Refresh graph, or the header refresh to see other-tab changes. This is snapshot data, not live collaboration. Ordinary internal-link navigation warns before discarding an unsaved draft. A failed navigation does not clear the draft guard; a failed detail refresh retains the previous note. Header refresh also checks for unsaved work. Browser history/navigation and crash recovery are not a durable draft system: save important changes first.
Graph Open Graph in navigation. It includes active/archived notes and excludes Trash. Filter titles or labels, choose one label, include/exclude archive, or focus a note and its immediate neighbours. Filters intersect; Reset filters returns the whole view. Fit graph frames the actual visible positions, including small graphs, and adapts to viewport size. Labels/dots retain a readable screen size while zooming. Camera buttons work with keyboard or touch; mouse dragging pans the background. The HTML note list and native focus selector provide equivalent navigation without requiring SVG interaction.
There is no continuous physics loop, animation tracking or network polling. A deterministic bounded layout is computed when graph data/filters change. At most 500 nodes and 1,000 directed edges are drawn; the current free account quota is still 250 notes. The node-limit control and an explicit warning disclose truncation. A reference beyond a note’s 256-reference limit is not counted as an edge/backlink; reduce or split that note to include it. Self-links remain valid but do not add graph edges or self-backlinks.
Try the same renderer without an account at /example/graph . Its six original notes are fixtures, with local anchor navigation; it reads no private API or cloud account and does not pretend to save user notes.
Implementation and operations /api/knowledge authenticates before database access, selects only the owner’s non-trashed rows and returns minimal derived metadata, not note bodies, account identifiers or credentials. Label ownership is checked too. The existing no-store/nosniff/CSP boundaries remain. Parsing uses pinned MIT-licensed mdast-util-from-markdown, mdast-util-gfm and micromark-extension-gfm, already shared with the Markdown toolchain. No HTML execution or wider image/network policy is added.
Metadata is fetched lazily when needed and kept only in the open workspace. Versioned/abortable requests reject stale responses; confirmed writes invalidate the snapshot. The route is bounded to 500 notes, with 30 requests/minute per account and 120/minute globally. Per-account admission happens before global admission so a single throttled account cannot consume the entire global counter. Fixed-window boundary bursts and provider-wide spending controls are not universal load/abuse certification.
No schema migration, original Keep database access, payment change, new provider or always-on service is required. Rollback to the Markdown/Vim release preserves bodies and ordinary account functionality; wiki syntax becomes text there. Source-bundle imports must later map imported identities explicitly rather than reusing another account’s IDs.
Primary parser references: from-markdown , GFM AST extensions , GFM syntax extensions . Installed package APIs and Next 16.3.8 client/route/lazy-loading guides were read before implementation. Current test/publication evidence belongs in connection release ; Firefox/Safari, physical touch/IME and formal accessibility certification remain separate checks.

Success consumes the complete quote; failure/cancellation/stale timeout releases it. Cleanup releases work exceeding the 20-minute deadline; a late worker cannot settle a released hold. Separate media/model/ledger volumes isolate state. Hourly cleanup deletes expired files and retains seven daily encrypted financial snapshots with media metadata removed. One speech container/coordinator and bounded uploads, rate limits, trial/admission/storage caps limit initial exposure. Estimated admission caps are not provider-wide hard spending limits. Storage, requests, failed work and schedules can still cost money.
Sonaweft and Pageweft share reviewed owned payment logic and currently an account-scoped Paddle runtime key, with distinct product/prices, notification secret, sessions, ledgers and volumes. They have no sibling runtime imports or shared customer wallet. Key rotation affects both until separate keys are configured.

description: Preview, validate and atomically import original exports, keep source assets and manage retention.
text:
Import, review, edit Export a fresh supported ZIP from Pageweft (plain, Obsidian or LLM preset) or Sonaweft. The original PDF/recording is included only if that exporter actually includes it. Keep your own original outside the service. Sign in to Noteweld and choose Source bundles. Select the ZIP and Validate and preview. This parses and verifies it without saving notes. Review filenames, categories, excerpts, file counts and archive SHA256. Original extraction, user corrections and AI notes retain distinct labels. Hashes validate internal consistency, not provenance authenticity, model accuracy or legal rights. Choose Use existing notes (default) or deliberately create another note copy. Confirm that you may retain the files, then Import all notes together. All notes and their immutable archive commit in one transaction. A failed import saves neither. Retrying a lost acknowledgement with the same operation ID does not duplicate notes. Open an imported note, edit and save normally. Private relative assets/source links resolve through owner-checked URLs; links between imported notes use stable internal IDs. Raw ZIP bytes remain unchanged. Your edited note is separate from its original source. Download the original ZIP any time within the preview’s artifact traffic allowance. Deleting a retained source preserves its notes but makes their source/asset links unavailable. Deleting your account removes both from live storage. Operator backups expire after seven days. Format and safety boundaries Supported: pageweft-export/v1 in MANIFEST.json with explicit files and notes; instascript-export/v1 in manifest.json for Sonaweft. Old Pageweft demonstration archives without the current schema/index need a fresh export. Arbitrary ZIPs, vaults and account/wallet migrations are not accepted.
Every payload must be declared exactly once with SHA256. Validation checks CRC, UTF-8 notes, entry count, actual expanded sizes, path traversal/absolute/control paths, case collisions, symlinks, encryption and unsupported compression. Files are parsed in memory, never extracted as executable paths. Unsupported/missing relative references fail before import. Raw HTML is skipped; private PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP assets may render, while external images remain deliberate links. Other retained content is served as a download with nosniff, restrictive CSP and no-store.
Preview limits ZIP ≤4 MiB; ≤1,000 entries; ≤16 MiB per expanded file; ≤32 MiB expanded total; bounded parse time. 1–250 imported Markdown notes; ≤100 KB per rewritten note; existing 250 notes/2 MiB text/account capacity applies to the whole transaction. Retained archive storage ≤8 MiB/account and ≤64 MiB across this free preview, measured from original compressed bytes (database/base64 overhead is additional). Artifact admission conservatively counts the whole archive, even when opening one asset: 32 MiB/account/day, 128 MiB/preview/day and 512 MiB/preview/fixed 30-day window. These protect the preview; they are not provider bill ceilings. Notes and source deletion remain available when a read allowance is exhausted. Daily counter maintenance retains 35 days to preserve monthly windows. Imports are limited to 20/hour/account. Confirmed copies consume note capacity but reuse one retained archive. Removing individual imported notes does not remove the archive; source deletion is separate. Support and recovery A 5xx response includes a support ID; report that ID without sending private documents or recovery keys. Retry rejected/failed imports only after reviewing the message. Lost passphrase recovery uses your saved private key or an actually configured, deliberately linked provider; email reset is not enabled. Source storage is not end-to-end encrypted. Do not keep sensitive or irreplaceable originals only in this preview.

Paddle approval does not complete Egyptian income-tax/banking paperwork. Activate deliberately after the above passes. Enable the existing notification destination with the setup key in the dashboard/API, preserving platform-only traffic and its stored signing secret. Redeploy with .venv/bin/python -m modal deploy app.py. Changing only a browser flag cannot enable billing. Do not open paid access before actual approval/test evidence. Controlled genuine purchase/refund: with the owner’s authorization and a known small charge, verify receipt, bound credit grant, recovery on another device, use/hold/settlement, partial/full refund revocation and the provider’s settlement record. The current work made no real payment. Confirm payout separately when it actually reaches the approved bank; do not equate a paid checkout with a bank deposit. Credential maintenance: both newly created API keys currently expire 13 January 2027. Rotate the runtime key before expiry (target 6 January); merge the new value into the existing payment secret and redeploy. Revoke the setup key after activation/provisioning tasks finish if it is no longer needed. Keep only the three required runtime permissions. Keep backups/key securely separate; never put private integration JSON files in Git/chat. Missed notifications and rollback Use .venv/bin/python -m scripts.reconcile_processing_orders with the owner Modal profile and current runtime environment credentials. It retries the durable inbox and reconciles namespaced Paddle purchases; it will not reinterpret old Lemon/fixture IDs as Paddle transactions. The hourly cleanup also retries pending events and checks up to 50 eligible least-recently-checked purchases. Public status polling can recover a missed initial grant only for a transaction belonging to that encrypted session’s original checkout intent. If processing was paid but no credit appears, retry status/support; do not pay again to refresh.
A refund after credit consumption can make the balance negative and block new work; completed output remains available until expiry. Investigate pending-event alerts and negative balances through the private operations report. Do not erase purchases or manually grant credits from a screenshot/transaction ID alone.
Rollback: disable billing first, pause the notification destination, restore the previous source and redeploy. Preserve the permanent volumes, encrypted session key and ledger. Payment intent/event tables are additive and older code can leave them in place. A fresh encrypted ledger snapshot was retrieved and its SQLite integrity/credit identities verified on 15 October 2026; it remains in ignored owner-only local storage. Acceptable Use Policy — software scope and prohibited stored-value/financial products; permission to sell this specific app still depends on review.
