text:
Original record: Book conversion release — 14 October 2026.
Implemented in the hosted Pageweft application; supersedes the one-page-only product and $1/month access proposal. Amir delegated a better pricing model and approved the conversion utility improvements. The public free sample remains one selected page, but inspection accepts books and paid jobs use separately funded credits.
Features and implementation Capability Implementation Books / ranges / batch inspection Up to five PDFs, each <=64 MiB and 1,000 source PDF pages; strict PDF validation and page-range parser; retained inspected PDFs can be resumed. Each conversion is separately confirmed. Preview and price before extraction Source page count, selected pages and text-layer samples are inspected without GPU work; fixed tariff quote must match the confirmation. Automatic / force OCR / cheaper text-only Pinned unmodified MinerU 2.7.6 uses its documented mode/language options; pypdf text-only worker uses no GPU and explicitly excludes OCR, image extraction and layout reconstruction. Bounded sections / partial recovery Selected pages split into groups of 20; at most two GPU workers. Successful sections survive failures; explicit retries select missing or chosen original pages and can force OCR. Duplicate requests cannot reserve or dispatch twice. Traceability / fidelity review Original page indices are mapped from the subset PDF back to the full source. Renderer preserves recognized headings, equations, HTML tables, captions, footnotes and images. Unhandled blocks, unmapped content, empty/short output, missing images and replacement glyphs are reported. Untouched engine output is retained separately; flags do not certify correctness. Corrections / history Plain Markdown editor with original-PDF page link, optimistic edit versions and saved history. Reprocessing retains user corrections. Engine text can be loaded explicitly into the editor draft. Portable outputs Single Markdown, individual pages, bounded page groups, or sections based on original PDF bookmarks. Local image paths, source hash, unavailable-page list, raw section extraction and review metadata. Source PDF inclusion is optional. Cancel / discard / delete / expiry Queued work releases reserved allowance. A running cancelled section may finish and be charged. Job deletion removes edits/output and releases an unshared source. Unused inspected sources can be discarded. Hourly cleanup removes 48-hour-expired files; balances/recovery persist separately. Account / purchase recovery Encrypted Secure/HttpOnly session; high-entropy recovery key stored only as keyed hash. One-time purchase keys can restore the owning account. No customer Modal credentials. Payments / refunds Separate one-time pack integration verifies scoped provider orders and signed events; duplicate orders grant once, full/partial refunds revoke pack credits. Atomic reserve/settle/release accounting in integer 1/10,000 USD units. Public test-mode grants disabled. Live seller configuration remains absent. The active HTTP factory is web/studio.py. web/main.py and web/billing.py preserve the retired interface/verifier for regression/compatibility work; they are not the public paid implementation. Books use /ledger/books.sqlite, separate from the original /ledger/state.sqlite. Each is owned by one serialized function. Do not run a second Modal app with a separate book_store function on the same volume. Owner verification scripts invoke deployed functions instead.
Pricing No recurring access fee. One-time $5/$10 processing packs; the service debit is:
MinerU: $0.50 service fee plus $0.005 per selected page. 100 pages = $1; 500 pages = $3; 1,000 pages = $5.50. Text layer only: $0.25 plus $0.001 per page. 500 pages = $0.75. This is a cheaper, explicitly more limited extraction route. Reprocessing already completed pages: $0.20 service fee plus the chosen method’s page rate. Failed-page retries do not repeat an already charged initial service fee. Failed sections release their page allowance. If no section succeeds, the service fee is released too. Existing successful work and its charges remain. These are launch service tariffs, not exact pass-through of a measured Modal invoice. Credits do not expire; files/edits do. Prepaid funds are not all profit when purchased. Taxes may be added at checkout; fees/support/refunds/compute reduce contribution. Recalibrate tariffs from representative actual bills before expanding spending limits.
Paddle fees supersede the historical Lemon-specific calculation: base 5% + $0.50/checkout. With no sales tax, $5 leaves $4.25 and $10 leaves $9 before processing/refunds/payout costs. Paddle calculates its fee from the tax-inclusive buyer total; actual tax mode and settlement must be checked. The savings come from amortizing a fixed transaction fee over prepaid use. Current financial assumptions and scenarios (local reference; not published) separate service debits, cash, costs and income.
Modal pricing : A10 $0.000306/sec, CPU $0.0000131/core/sec, RAM $0.00000222/GiB/sec. New GPU sections request/cap two CPU cores and 8 GiB RAM, with 240-second function timeout, 180-second extraction bound and 5-second scale-down window. Model load, waiting, storage and orchestration can add cost. This is not invoice measurement or a guarantee every PDF finishes within the bound.
Initial safety limits: 100 retained-document creations/day globally; five retained inspected documents per owner; GPU page attempts 3,000/day globally and 2,000/owner/day, text attempts 30,000/day globally and 5,000/owner/day. Failed attempts still count toward safety limits, despite credit refunds. Trial capped at 3/day and 20/month globally, once per owner/IP. Shared-IP restrictions can affect legitimate users. These caps protect initial owner spending and must be deliberately calibrated for growth; no thousands-of-concurrent-user capacity claim is made.
Owner operations addition The private owner report now retrieves actual Modal workspace billing, separates verified commercial funding from fixtures, retains cumulative service consumption across file cleanup and checks credit identities. Atomic admission envelopes default to $10/day and $25/UTC month, at $0.15/GPU or $0.01/text section attempt. These are provisional controls, not a provider invoice cap. Pause blocks new/queued dispatch with an explicit allowance release; running work may complete. Rate quotas, 64 KiB JSON bounds and a separate CPU/memory/time-bounded PDF inspector harden the HTTP path. Read OPERATIONS.md and LAUNCH.md for the outer provider spending limit and actual payment/account/customer evidence.
Existing hourly cleanup adds bounded refund reconciliation, encrypted financial snapshots without document text/filenames, and sanitized rule-based alerts. Off-platform financial backup decryption/integrity/credit identities are checked on a disposable clone, not by overwriting production. No email alert or third-party analytics service was connected. An original public PDF/Markdown/ZIP guide and crawl metadata are available; indexing and sales are not established.
Evidence Automated suite: 60 unique checks, including real 1,000-page PDF inspection/end-section extraction, timeout/funds lifecycle, actual PDF-bookmark exports, refund cancellation, retry replay and malformed-request tests. Real Modal MinerU: original four-page PDF, selected pages 1/3/4, produced mapped portable output. This was an owner-authenticated internal credit fixture, not a purchase. Real deployed CPU: the complete original 1,000-page synthetic PDF processed across 50 sections via deployed book_store/run_book functions, with fixture credit and no second ledger writer. Final archive has all 1,000 ordered source pages, zero unavailable pages and the correct $1.25 service-credit debit. Four-page source selection was also checked. This is text-layer extraction of a synthetic PDF, not a scanned-book or technical-fidelity benchmark, and not a customer payment. Real public HTTP: inspection of pages 3–4, unfunded confirmation rejected with 409, one-page sample delivered original page 3, edit saved, corrected per-page ZIP downloaded with source PDF omitted, other session denied. Local Chromium: real PDF text extraction and explicit local seeded credit at widths 320/390/768/1440; quote, confirmation, correction history, selective reprocessing and ZIP download passed; no horizontal overflow/page errors. Batch inspection checked at 320/1440. Browser fixture does not verify payments or local GPU extraction. Actual seller checkout, provider test-mode webhook delivery, funds arrival, payout and a representative difficult-book comparison are not verified. No claim of perfect OCR, fixed damaged IPA or superior extraction is made. Ignored artifacts contain sanitized evidence/synthetic PDFs; source books and secrets are not added. Screenshots and browser errors are private test artifacts. No new local AI model was installed and no NixOS configuration was changed.

description: Offline text scoring, explicit unknown costs, failure-inclusive timings and representative-sample requirements.
text:
Offline scoring scripts/score_quality.py compares human-prepared comparable text and observed measurements. It never uploads files, calls a model, spends credits or silently changes app limits. It reports exact character/word edit rates, not factual correctness or a calibrated confidence badge. Case, punctuation, numeric values, diacritics and technical symbols remain significant; only Unicode NFC and CRLF representation normalize. Whitespace splits word tokens, so CER is generally the more useful measure for languages without space-delimited words.
Create a private ignored directory, e.g. .local/benchmarks/run-01/. Keep the permission/original-source basis, exact engine/model/resource settings and original source. Never publish a book/recording just because a benchmark needs it. Prepare a checked reference and comparable candidate text for each selected page/segment. Exclude the same export wrapper/front matter on both sides deliberately; the scorer does not guess what content to strip. Include omitted and repeated material in the aligned reference rather than cherry-picking clean output. Record each source SHA256, actual timings, retries/failed work, correction minutes and attributable processing costs. Unknown costs/counts must remain null, not zero. Add failed cases so cost/timing totals do not hide them. Separately record significant number/symbol errors, missing/duplicate units and timing errors from human review; exact text distance cannot infer these reliably. Run .venv/bin/python scripts/score_quality.py PRIVATE_MANIFEST --output NEW_PRIVATE_REPORT.json. The output is created exclusively with0600 permissions. It includes manifest/source/reference/candidate hashes, denominators, observation counts and explicit unknowns. It never overwrites another run. Keep the manifest alongside the report. Read both completed/failed counts and known-cost coverage before interpreting averages. P50/p95 use linearly interpolated order statistics over known wall timings, including failures. Tiny/selected samples do not establish production percentiles. Service debit is not cash revenue; attributable compute is not total cost or profit. Manifest All files must be inside the manifest’s directory. Sources may be≤64MiB; each comparable UTF-8 text≤200KB. Exact edit work is capped at25million cells: split long documents/recordings into predefined comparable pages/segments. Maximum100cases/run. These are offline tool bounds, not revised hosted limits.
{ "schema": "processing-benchmark/v1", "product": "sonaweft", "cases": [{ "id": "audio-001", "permission_note": "Actual original/permission/license basis", "pipeline": "Actual engine/model revision; CPU/GPU, memory, routing, retries", "status": "completed", "source_file": "source.mp3", "source_sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_SHA256", "reference_file": "reference.txt", "candidate_file": "candidate.txt", "wall_seconds": null, "cold_load_seconds": null, "idle_seconds": null, "correction_minutes": null, "service_debit_usd": null, "provider_cost_usd": null, "timestamp_mae_seconds": null, "missing_units": null, "duplicate_units": null, "significant_symbol_errors": null }] } This is an unfilled template, not a measured result. A failed case uses status: failed, omits reference/candidate and still records known time/cost. Amounts are USD. The offline report contains source identifiers/resource labels; keep it private until deliberately reviewed. A recorded permission note does not itself prove legal permission.
Required measurement sets PDF: digital text, scans, old print, multiple columns, tables/equations, figures/captions, footnotes, IPA/diacritics and long-book joins. Check page coverage, reading order, assets, numbers/symbols and correction time against the actual source. Compare text/MinerU routes on the same permission-cleared tasks; then compare the owner’s alternatives with the same reference, scope, correction task and complete costs. No competitor or long-book accuracy result is asserted here.
Audio: use product: sonaweft; prepare aligned5/30/60-minute clean/noisy/accented/technical/multi-speaker sets. Measure segment omission/repetition/timing, human correction minutes, cold/idle/runtime, failures/retries and provider token/model data. Do not infer speaker identity, meaning or factual correctness from WER.
The five synthetic scorer tests verify calculations, unknown-cost handling, failed-work inclusion, source/path/measurement rejection and symbol-preserving normalization. They do not benchmark OCR/ASR. Actual representative samples, human references/review and provider-bill allocation remain required before claiming quality, throughput or margins.

description: Compare and restore saved corrections and speaker labels, retain hashed history exports, and understand deletion and expiry.
text:
Sonaweft keeps the original machine transcript unchanged. Corrections and speaker labels are your annotations. Their latest 20 saved states now survive a reload or recovered workspace, for as long as the recording itself remains available.
Use saved history Open a completed result with Review & export. Expand Saved edit history and choose Load saved history. Choose a version. Changed passages show the current saved text/label beside the selected version. Reading history never replaces the editor draft. Save any unfinished correction or speaker label first. Select Restore this version as a new save and confirm the scope: every annotation in this result, rather than only the passage currently selected. Restoration creates a new revision. Retained earlier saves and the original ASR remain available; another tab cannot silently overwrite a newer revision. The comparison is plain inert text, including source material that resembles HTML. The current save is marked explicitly. A result changed in another tab must be reopened before restoring; failed requests preserve the saved result and draft. Inputs are temporarily disabled during an annotation write to prevent lost typing. Refreshing listening/glossary cues preserves both drafts instead of resetting the editor, and a response for an earlier result cannot change the newly opened one.
Portability and retention The complete ZIP includes annotation-history.json, identified as sonaweft-annotations/v1 and covered by the export manifest’s SHA-256 hashes. It contains the retained snapshots, revision numbers, actions and available save times. Restore records identify the revision restored. Imported legacy results start with their real existing state; the app does not fabricate earlier edits or an unknown last-save date. Noteweld retains this file with the original bundle; it does not import the snapshots as separate notes or offer Sonaweft restoration.
History has the same source ownership and expiry as the result: normally 48 hours. Deleting a recording removes its annotation rows and clears both current corrections and speaker labels. Expiry cleanup also removes the snapshots. Financial backups exclude transcript corrections, labels and their history. Downloading a bundle is necessary if you want a longer-lived personal copy. It is not an indefinite hosted archive or a financial/audit record.
Each result has a 256 KiB combined annotation-state limit and at most 20 retained states. Very large exports still have to meet the destination’s import limits; Noteweld currently accepts ZIP files up to 4 MiB with its existing note/file quotas.
Returning to a full-recording quote After inspecting an interval, choose Use the full recording. The server re-quotes that same upload; the app does not duplicate the file, calculate a different tariff locally or start processing. The first-30-second sample becomes eligible only if it still meets the existing mode, workspace, IP and global quotas. Returning to the full recording never resets a consumed trial allowance.
Implementation and verification sonaweft_web/annotations.py stores snapshots in the existing serialized SQLite writer. Annotation changes, snapshots and retention pruning share one transaction; a failed snapshot rolls back the current annotation too. History reads and restore require the owned, completed, unexpired result. Restore also requires CSRF verification, a current expected revision and the annotation rate limit. Boolean/malformed revisions are rejected. ledger.py integrates history with source deletion, cleanup and content-free financial snapshots. app.py registers only the three named store operations; the HTTP boundary does not expose a generic ledger operation endpoint. Real SQLite/HTTP tests cover recovery, migration from existing revisions, conflicts, retention, invalid input, cross-workspace isolation, deletion, rollback, backup exclusion and original-ASR-preserving hashed exports. DOM tests cover stale responses, draft safety, explicit restore, inert text and request failure. Real Chromium tests use local SQLite and media decoding with an explicitly replayed original demo ASR; they do not claim new transcription accuracy, provider payments or external OAuth acceptance. Browser review covers 320/390/768/1440 widths and automated WCAG A/AA checks on the review panel. Real people, physical devices and Safari remain separate evidence. Motion respects reduced-motion settings, and entry animation is restricted to the review header rather than a large composited editor surface. For a repeatable browser run, start scripts.preview_source:app with a fresh private SONAWEFT_PREVIEW_DIR. Reusing an old preview can correctly exhaust the real trial quota; do not raise production allowances to make tests pass. Then run node scripts/source-review.browser.cjs against its loopback URL. The fixture accepts only the original public example recording and makes no model/payment call. Alternatively, .venv-web/bin/python scripts/run_source_review.py creates its own private fresh ledger and loopback port, waits for readiness, runs the journey, retains its evidence and stops only the server it started.
This improves recoverability and continuity of source review. It is not a claim that version history is unique to Sonaweft, or that accuracy, demand and profitability have been established. Billing activation remains a separate verified milestone.

description: Offline text scoring, explicit unknown costs, failure-inclusive timings and representative-sample requirements.
text:
Offline scoring scripts/score_quality.py compares human-prepared comparable text and observed measurements. It never uploads files, calls a model, spends credits or silently changes app limits. It reports exact character/word edit rates, not factual correctness or a calibrated confidence badge. Case, punctuation, numeric values, diacritics and technical symbols remain significant; only Unicode NFC and CRLF representation normalize. Whitespace splits word tokens, so CER is generally the more useful measure for languages without space-delimited words.
Create a private ignored directory, e.g. .local/benchmarks/run-01/. Keep the permission/original-source basis, exact engine/model/resource settings and original source. Never publish a book/recording just because a benchmark needs it. Prepare a checked reference and comparable candidate text for each selected page/segment. Exclude the same export wrapper/front matter on both sides deliberately; the scorer does not guess what content to strip. Include omitted and repeated material in the aligned reference rather than cherry-picking clean output. Record each source SHA256, actual timings, retries/failed work, correction minutes and attributable processing costs. Unknown costs/counts must remain null, not zero. Add failed cases so cost/timing totals do not hide them. Separately record significant number/symbol errors, missing/duplicate units and timing errors from human review; exact text distance cannot infer these reliably. Run .venv/bin/python scripts/score_quality.py PRIVATE_MANIFEST --output NEW_PRIVATE_REPORT.json. The output is created exclusively with0600 permissions. It includes manifest/source/reference/candidate hashes, denominators, observation counts and explicit unknowns. It never overwrites another run. Keep the manifest alongside the report. Read both completed/failed counts and known-cost coverage before interpreting averages. P50/p95 use linearly interpolated order statistics over known wall timings, including failures. Tiny/selected samples do not establish production percentiles. Service debit is not cash revenue; attributable compute is not total cost or profit. Manifest All files must be inside the manifest’s directory. Sources may be≤64MiB; each comparable UTF-8 text≤200KB. Exact edit work is capped at25million cells: split long documents/recordings into predefined comparable pages/segments. Maximum100cases/run. These are offline tool bounds, not revised hosted limits.
{ "schema": "processing-benchmark/v1", "product": "pageweft", "cases": [{ "id": "digital-001", "permission_note": "Actual original/permission/license basis", "pipeline": "Actual engine/model revision; CPU/GPU, memory, routing, retries", "status": "completed", "source_file": "source.pdf", "source_sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_SHA256", "reference_file": "reference.txt", "candidate_file": "candidate.txt", "wall_seconds": null, "cold_load_seconds": null, "idle_seconds": null, "correction_minutes": null, "service_debit_usd": null, "provider_cost_usd": null, "timestamp_mae_seconds": null, "missing_units": null, "duplicate_units": null, "significant_symbol_errors": null }] } This is an unfilled template, not a measured result. A failed case uses status: failed, omits reference/candidate and still records known time/cost. Amounts are USD. The offline report contains source identifiers/resource labels; keep it private until deliberately reviewed. A recorded permission note does not itself prove legal permission.
Required measurement sets PDF: digital text, scans, old print, multiple columns, tables/equations, figures/captions, footnotes, IPA/diacritics and long-book joins. Check page coverage, reading order, assets, numbers/symbols and correction time against the actual source. Compare text/MinerU routes on the same permission-cleared tasks; then compare the owner’s alternatives with the same reference, scope, correction task and complete costs. No competitor or long-book accuracy result is asserted here.
Audio: use product: sonaweft; prepare aligned5/30/60-minute clean/noisy/accented/technical/multi-speaker sets. Measure segment omission/repetition/timing, human correction minutes, cold/idle/runtime, failures/retries and provider token/model data. Do not infer speaker identity, meaning or factual correctness from WER.
The five synthetic scorer tests verify calculations, unknown-cost handling, failed-work inclusion, source/path/measurement rejection and symbol-preserving normalization. They do not benchmark OCR/ASR. Actual representative samples, human references/review and provider-bill allocation remain required before claiming quality, throughput or margins.

description: Attach, preview, retain, download and delete private note media.
text:
Add a file to a note Choose Upload to → Noteweld storage or Google Drive, then attach, paste or drop one supported file into the editor attachment area. Connect Drive separately in Account first. The destination is remembered per account in this browser; failed uploads never silently switch providers. Save the note after insertion. Preview shows supported images and native audio/video players; codec support depends on the browser.
Images can be up to 10 MB and audio/video up to 25 MB per file. The free account allowance is 100 MB, with at most 500 attachments. Managed files live in private Cloudflare R2 storage with a recovery copy; Drive originals remain in the connected Google Drive and do not consume managed bytes; account permissions control reads. Notes and media are not end-to-end encrypted.
Keep or remove files Open Account → Manage storage and plan → Manage stored attachments to download or remove a file. Removing only its Markdown reference keeps the reusable original in the library. Deleting the library file affects every note using it. Download anything important first.
Account JSON includes an attachment manifest, not the actual media bytes; download those separately. Archived/trashed notes and unfinished reservations still count. Shared availability can temporarily pause uploads without disclosing private accounting.
Evidence Actual public HTTPS checks passed original-byte storage/recovery, private access and foreign-account refusal, ranges, native image/audio/video playback, saved-note reload, invalid/oversize rejection and explicit deletion. This does not certify every browser codec or an unlimited hosting allowance.
Storage and plan behavior explains usage and over-limit recovery.
Drive uploads, retries and privacy explains direct uploads and original retention.
title: Images, audio and video

description: Usage, reserved bytes, file management, planned Plus and safe downgrade.
text:
Find your usage Open Account → Manage storage and plan . The panel shows saved files, unfinished uploads, pending removals and remaining space. Free includes 100 MB and at most 500 attachments; images can be up to 10 MB, audio/video up to 25 MB each.
Reservations and unfinished removals count until released. Archived/trashed notes still count. Expand the library to download ready files or remove an unneeded file/reservation. Removal warns that any note using the file will show an unavailable attachment. Refresh retries a failed read; stale displayed values are labeled.
More storage and changes of plan Plus is planned at $5/month for 5 GB. Subscriptions are not available yet; no payment or production upgrade is implied by a local sandbox test.
When files exceed the current allowance, new uploads pause. Notes, existing-file downloads and deletion remain available. Plan expiry does not automatically delete saved files. Account JSON contains a metadata manifest. For current notes and actual available media together, choose Account → Keep a copy → Download Markdown vault.
Verification Unit and actual isolated database tests cover charged reservations, current-plan admission, local sandbox Plus, expiry and retained read/delete access. Browser checks cover local download/removal/reclaimed quota, failure/retry, themes and separately mocked full/unavailable states. Independent review approved the local interface. The deployed account screen and quota metadata passed a documented temporary operator-session check; its session was removed. Encrypted pre/post snapshots restored with original durable data unchanged. Real commercial billing remains a separate gate.
Using Noteweld is the normal starting point. Private operating budgets, credentials and internal admission configuration are omitted.
Google Drive and private servers Choose Google Drive in a note to upload originals directly to your own Drive allowance; those bytes do not consume managed storage, while references still count toward the combined attachment limit. A separate source-distributed owner-operated server profile adds authenticated encrypted attachment storage. It is not a third destination in the hosted menu and does not provide user-held-key end-to-end encryption. Private-server scope . Media/storage choices .
title: Storage usage and plans

description: Email-first signup, address verification and mailed password recovery.
text:
Create and recover an account Open Account to sign in with an existing passphrase. New email signup requests a link; explicitly choosing a passphrase on its confirmation form creates the credential. Opening a link alone does not create it. Existing unverified accounts can verify their address from their owned, recently authenticated workspace. Equal addresses never merge workspaces.
Verified addresses can request mailed resets. Completion revokes previous sessions and invalidates old recovery keys. Links expire after thirty minutes and work once; opening/previewing does not consume them. A separate saved key is optional when verified email recovery is available. Keep any key private.
Confirmation in another browser explicitly creates a fresh workspace. Guest files/credits remain in the original browser without implicit transfer. A passphrase or existing private key confirms ownership for sensitive session/provider actions.
Providers and availability Google/GitHub identity flows have local state/nonce/PKCE tests; dedicated registrations and genuine consent acceptance remain separate. Absent providers stay hidden. Accounts are product-specific. Signing in does not reset free eligibility or open checkout. Email verification, CSRF and throttles are active; an IP/cookie is not verified human identity. Unavailable processing returns Currently unavailable. Please try again later. Owner accounting stays private.
The deployed release passed real synthetic Resend issuance and actual HTTPS confirmation/reset/replay refusal, old-session revocation, ownership proof and readiness. Fixtures were removed and original data preserved through encrypted pre/post restores. A synthetic receipt is not a human inbox or OAuth-consent check. No GPU/payment job ran for this acceptance.
title: Verified email and recovery

description: Planned storage subscriptions and the distinction between test and real payments.
text:
Current availability Subscriptions and live checkout remain disabled. The current free preview includes 100 MB of managed media. Plus is planned at $5/month for 5 GB; planned capacity is not an active purchase offer.
Preparation is not a real payment Paddle sandbox server preparation and isolated tests cover protected checkout intents, signed-event validation, duplicates, ordered state, reconciliation and owner boundaries. Local sandbox Plus storage tests never grant production storage or prove an actual purchase.
Merchant approval, actual sandbox checkout delivery, commercial capacity, live activation and payment/payout acceptance remain separate. The interface must not take a payment while checkout is unavailable.
Storage and plans describes today’s limits and safe over-limit behavior. Owner verification documents, provider credentials and private operating budgets are excluded from this public edition.
title: Subscription availability

description: Choose Noteweld storage or your Google Drive for attachments, paste and drop.
text:
Choose where new files go In a signed-in note, use Upload to → Noteweld storage or Google Drive. Then use Attach media, paste an image or drop a file. Connect Google Drive separately under Account → Google Drive first. The destination is remembered for your account in this browser; it is not synchronized between devices.
Drive originals upload directly from your browser to your connected Google Drive. Noteweld verifies their type and bytes and inserts private references. Save the note. Use the Google Drive panel and Choose or upload in Drive for files already in Drive.
Limits and recovery The free preview includes 100 MB of managed Noteweld media. Drive originals use your Google allowance and do not consume managed bytes. Images may be up to 10 MB; supported audio/video up to 25 MB. The account has a combined 500-attachment limit, with up to 100 references per note. Delivery has additional traffic/concurrency safeguards. Paid plans and checkout remain disabled.
A failed Drive upload never falls back to Noteweld storage. Keep the note open and use the destination-specific retry. Reloading or closing the editor clears in-memory retry state. If an upload completed but insertion failed, its original may already exist in Drive: select it through the Drive panel rather than uploading another copy.
Removing a Drive reference leaves the original in Google Drive; removing a managed attachment reclaims its Noteweld storage and makes it unavailable in notes using it. Download individual originals or use Account → Keep a copy → Download Markdown vault to collect current notes and actual available files together. Externally changed Drive files require explicit replacement confirmation.
Privacy and unfinished features These options are private to the signed-in account, but are not end-to-end encrypted. The application verifies and serves the selected bytes. Drive access uses a separate, narrow file grant; Google sign-in alone does not connect storage. Local-vault sync uses explicit previews and conflict decisions. The separately qualified Linux desktop alpha adds offline files and actual Neovim; it does not execute Obsidian plugins. A source-distributed private-server profile supplies a separate installation with administrator-held encryption keys, not a third hosted destination or E2EE.
Return to Using Noteweld .
title: Images, audio, video and storage

description: Compare and restore bounded saved revisions.
text:
Compare and restore Open a saved note, choose History, select a version and compare it with the current content. Download its Markdown or confirm Restore this version. Restore creates a new revision; newer concurrent edits are refused rather than overwritten.
Free recovery retains up to ten revisions per note for fourteen days, within 8 MiB compressed history per account. Older entries can expire sooner under pressure. Existing notes begin capturing history on their next edit; past versions are not fabricated. Permanent deletion removes history. Separately deleted media, disconnected Drive grants and unsaved text cannot be recreated. Vault exports contain current content, not full history.
Snapshots include text, checklist and note properties. Standalone label-setting changes are not note revisions. Restore a trashed note from Trash first. Keep independent exports.
The deployed release exercised real PostgreSQL ownership, conflict/retention/corruption/rollback checks, browser comparisons/downloads/restore and actual public password/cookie restoration. Encrypted pre/post restores preserved original durable data. This is bounded recovery, not unlimited backup or crash-proof drafts.
title: Recover saved versions

description: Keyboard search, capture templates and saved-note navigation.
text:
Find saved work Choose Find & commands in the header. Outside editable fields, Ctrl+K (Linux/Windows) or Cmd+K (macOS) opens it. Inside the editor use the header button so the editor keeps its keys. Type title, passage, checklist or label words; all words must match. Filter by label or include Archive; Trash is excluded. At most twenty results appear.
Arrows/Enter choose, Tab reaches filters and Escape restores focus. Opening a note focuses its title. Links/backlinks and Back to notes continue navigation. Ctrl/Cmd+S saves inside the editor; failure retains the draft.
Capture safely With no phrase, choose New blank note, New source note or New decision note. Templates provide editable prompts, not generated claims. A nonempty draft is focused rather than replaced. Unsaved-work confirmation remains active.
Search matches bounded literal text within the signed-in account. It uses no embeddings/inference service. Failure preserves the phrase/filters for Retry. Hosted acceptance exercised search, archive/labels, capture/save, dirty drafts, links and anonymous refusal. Chromium checks also exercised keyboard, network retry and scoped accessibility.
title: Find, capture and navigate

description: Preview ZIP imports and export notes with actual files.
text:
Import a folder In Source bundles, choose Markdown or Obsidian vault ZIP. ZIP only intended material, removing credentials/private configuration first. Validate, inspect and confirm. Preview creates no notes; application is atomic and idempotent within the limits.
Original archives remain separate/downloadable. Editable copies retain frontmatter/source text and map supported references to owned notes/files. Missing/ambiguous targets are not guessed. Configuration/plugins remain inert; this is not an Obsidian plugin runtime.
Keep a readable copy Account → Keep a copy → Download Markdown vault collects current notes/checklists, available stored attachments, retained sources and original ZIPs, with relative links and a state/hash manifest. Unsaved drafts, full past-version history, arbitrary remote media and credentials are excluded. A missing/corrupt/disconnected stored file fails collection explicitly; restore access and retry. Account JSON is separate metadata.
Imports are bounded to 4 MiB ZIP, 1,000 entries, 32 MiB expanded, 250 notes, 2 MiB note text and 8 MiB retained sources per account. Export is bounded to 192 MiB/4,096 files, transfer admission and a two-minute stream deadline. Hosted import/export exercised original bytes, R2 media and export hashes, including reimport without resurrecting deliberately deleted editable notes. Local sync is separate.
title: Markdown and Obsidian vaults

description: Pair a folder and preview transfers with recoverable conflicts.
text:
Connect deliberately The source CLI needs Node.js 24.13+ and locked dependencies. Connect a chosen Markdown folder to a compatible server, open the printed URL in your browser and approve the named device/scope in Account → Devices & agents. Never enter passwords/recovery keys into an agent or pairing prompt. Grants expire after 90 days and can be revoked earlier.
Prepare/download the initial snapshot, review and confirm its digest. Preparation does not overwrite visible files. For an existing Obsidian vault, first import its ZIP on the website and explicitly adopt that source. Exact commands are provided with the access-controlled source.
Daily work and conflicts Edit locally online or offline. Preview pushes/pulls/conflicts, then confirm that exact preview. Divergent edits retain local text plus a separate cloud copy for an explicit decision. Local deletion never silently deletes a cloud note; cloud deletion never silently erases a local file. Adopt deliberate renames before editing moved content. New local notes require include-new preview. Keep the sync journal when moving the vault.
New local media uses managed storage with existing limits, without silently falling back to Drive. Plugins/configuration are not executed. Reader scopes read, Agent scopes propose for review, and Sync scopes read/update notes/files. None manages account settings, providers or billing. Scopes cover the complete account, not selected folders.
Credentials live outside the vault in private files, not an encrypted keychain. Revocation blocks future access but does not erase downloaded files. Reset/sign-out-all invalidates grants; restored clients reconnect. Actual CLI/PostgreSQL/browser and hosted journeys exercised two-way edits, conflicts, R2 bytes, new notes and revocation. See the separately qualified desktop alpha .
title: Local vault sync and devices

description: Allow reading and proposed changes with separate human acceptance.
text:
Review before accepting An explicitly paired Agent can list/read owned notes and submit complete Markdown creation/update proposals. It cannot approve itself, directly delete notes, manage providers or billing. Open Account → Devices & agents → Review agent proposals, compare the text/reason, then accept or reject. Accepted work uses ordinary ownership, revisions, quotas and history. A stale revision or revoked/expired device refuses acceptance. Checklist updates are unsupported.
The optional stdio MCP bridge exposes list_notes, read_note, propose_note and proposal_status. Device bearer access is separate from browser cookies; only the authenticated owner approves. Installation does not pair an account or change a model. Portable human/agent instructions accompany the source.
Grants expire after 90 days and cover the entire account. Drafts/receipts expire after seven days, with bounded counts, bytes and submission rates. Backups retain accepted notes/history but omit grants and pending proposals. Real DeepTutor MCP transport, CLI, PostgreSQL and browser decisions were exercised without invoking a model or changing its account/configuration. Hosted checks covered read/propose, review/history, duplicate/stale refusal and revocation; they do not create another owner’s grant.
title: Reviewed agent proposals

description: Offline Markdown with actual Neovim and optional cloud sync.
text:
Local files and your real editor The source-distributed unsigned Linux x64 alpha opens an ordinary Markdown/Obsidian folder. No account is needed for offline reading, full-text search, links/backlinks, Connections, note templates and supported local media. Refresh files updates indexes after another app edits files. Start with a copy of valuable work and keep independent backups.
Edit in nvim opens the actual editor in a split pane; Expand editor enlarges the same process. Use :w to save and :wq to save/close. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F6 returns focus to app controls. Settings accepts an executable plus separate arguments, not a shell command string. Neovim uses its normal configuration/plugins and local-user permissions beyond the renderer sandbox.
A checked working copy protects the original; written edits are verified before replacement. Concurrent edits preserve both, and written work can recover after restart. Unwritten keystrokes are not recoverable. Remote images are not automatically loaded and the viewer does not run Obsidian plugins.
Preferences, setup and limits Optional cloud sync requires browser approval and exact transfer confirmation. Credentials stay outside the vault in private files, not an encrypted keychain. Six palettes, light/dark/system, reading font/size and 32 app color roles save locally; Neovim colors/keymaps remain its own settings.
The owner-access source contains Node 24, native dependency, runtime/build and launch instructions. This page does not distribute an installer/private source. Thirteen actual Linux scenarios, packaged SQLite/PTY/Neovim, written restart recovery, scoped accessibility and hosted two-way sync/revocation passed. Independent finish review accepted the two listed corrections. macOS/Windows packages, signing, auto-update and every editor plugin remain unqualified.
title: Linux desktop alpha

description: Review source-grounded text cards with stable import identities.
text:
Preview, export, import The optional source CLI accepts explicitly authored card batches with a stable external ID, question/answer, local source path, exact file hash and verbatim supporting quote. It checks visible vault bytes before export. Human review still determines accuracy and useful retrieval; a matching quote alone does not make a good card.
Preview the batch, inspect its digest and confirm export to a new UTF-8 tab-separated file. Active HTML and Anki sound syntax are escaped. No model call, Noteweld account or AnkiWeb credential is needed.
Create Noteweld Recall v1 in Anki with fields NoteweldID, Question, Answer, Source, NoteweldID first, and one Recall card template. Import into the intended deck, review field mapping/duplicate-update settings and confirm. Keep IDs stable on later imports to update the same notes/cards while preserving scheduling. Omitted cards are not deleted. Exact CLI/template/agent instructions accompany the source.
This is text-only: no app export button, automatic live-deck writes, synthetic ratings, cloze/image/audio generation or duplicate FSRS. Anki owns scheduling. Installed Anki 26.09.3 imported real CLI output three times into a temporary collection; one synthetic review and later text updates preserved note/card IDs, checked scheduling fields and exact review rows. The owner’s profile/AnkiWeb were untouched.
title: Anki text-card handoff

description: Separate deployment with encrypted attachments and explicit recovery.
text:
Separate installation This source profile runs a separate compatible Noteweld instance. It does not provision a public server, add a third hosted upload destination or provide unlimited paid storage. Desktop/CLI clients select a compatible origin and pair to that server’s account; existing accounts/files do not move automatically.
An administrator supplies PostgreSQL, a fixed HTTPS origin and private directories. Setup generates private configuration/independent keys. Migrations require an explicit target. Owner bootstrap is limited to an empty account table and does not mark email verified. Email, OAuth, DNS/TLS, public deployment and independent backup custody need separate configuration and acceptance. Billing stays disabled.
Privacy and recovery Attachments use authenticated AES-256-GCM envelopes tied to object identity, with primary/recovery copies. Reads authenticate before plaintext/ranges; a missing/corrupt primary can use an authenticated recovery file. Paths are fixed administrator configuration, not untrusted note URLs. Permissions, symlinks, hashes and sizes are checked.
The server holds keys: this is encryption at rest, not E2EE. Notes, PostgreSQL/WAL, source imports and temporary files still need encrypted OS storage. Two directories on one disk are not off-device disaster recovery. Protect and independently retain keys.
Encrypted database backup uses a separate key; restore requires an explicitly selected new empty database. Media bytes, live sessions/devices and pending proposals are excluded. Keep a coherent database/object copy plus independent keys; reconnect clients/Drive after restore. Wrong keys, damaged snapshots, the live target and nonempty targets are refused.
Actual local PostgreSQL bootstrap/owner creation/backup/restore, corruption/identity/range checks, media cleanup/accounting and a production-browser encrypted-media journey passed. No public customer server, reverse proxy, off-device backup or key rotation was provisioned/certified. Human/agent runbooks and example service/proxy files accompany the source.
title: Owner-operated private server
